To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the 3′ splicing of the CBS intron 7 is regulated by the interaction of a trans-acting factor with the G repeats of the 3' splice site, that a duplication of this region has created a gene re- arrangement at the 3' end of intron 8, and that this re-arrangement has acquired the ability to interact with a specific trans- acting factor that favors the selection of the original distal 3' splice.
the 844insG allele, which is associated to hyperhomocysteinemia, is a polymorphism that consists in the insertion of a 68 bp sequence that duplicates the 3′-splice site and the 5’-end of exon8.

the 844insG allele of the CBS gene is associated with a higher risk of homocysteinemia, and that the insertion is the cause of a gene re-configuration that leads to the selection of the correct 3′ splice-site.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanism by which the 844ins duplication affects 3′ splice-site selection in the CBS gene.
the mechanism of selection of the 844ins variant in the CBS gene, which is associated with hyperhomocysteinemia, a condition that is a risk factor for vascular diseases.
the regulation of 3′ splice selection in the 844 ins68 polymorphism of the human CBS gene.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

844ins68 polymorphism is a complex phenomenon that involves the regulation of alternative splicing, the generation of a new binding site for a trans-acting factor, the disruption of the reading frame and the creation of an in-frame stop codon, which all contribute to the generation of a functional variant of the CBS gene.
the 844insG allele has been selected by natural evolution as a mechanism for the regulation of 3′ splice selection in the CBS gene.
the insertion of 68 bp has created a new binding site for a splicing factor that is able to compete with the proximal 5′ splice site, thus favoring the distal selection of the 844insG allele.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the 844ins 68 polymorphism is a consequence of the duplication of the 3' splice site of introns 7 and 8 of the CBS gene.
the 844ins 68 polymorphism of the CBS gene is a rare event that might be a consequence of a gene re- arrangement that occurred during evolution.
the 844insG68 polymorphism is a rare example of a gene re-configuration that has not led to the production of a deleterious protein.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a duplication of a 3′ splice acceptor site in a gene can be an evolutionary event that allows the rescue of the original gene, so preserving protein functionality.
the 844insG allele is not a neutral mutation but that it has been selected for its ability to maintain the wild-type sequence and function of CBS.
the duplication has created an hnRNP H-binding motif that has acquired the ability to regulate 3′ splice-site selection.
